transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I came in because... it's just getting really hard to talk to people at work. I'm a jeweler, and people will ask me a really simple question, like, you know, when a ring repair will be ready. And I try to answer, but my answer just starts going from the repair invoices to... well, the invoices have been a mess lately anyway, the paper they use now is so thin. I actually used a stack of old ones to line the bottom of my planters for my garden soil, because you need good drainage for tomatoes. If the soil stays too wet, the roots just rot. But then the soil reminded me of the yard, and how I need to find the mortgage papers because I was looking for them last week... and I'll be saying all this out loud to the customer who just wanted their ring, and I can just see them losing me. They just stare at me. I don't know why I can't just keep it simple anymore.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually energized and needed much less sleep than usual?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I usually sleep okay, mostly. Actually, I was looking at beds the other day because my mattress is getting this dip right in the middle, you know? It's one of those memory foam ones, and they say they bounce back, but I don't think they really do. I bought it maybe five years ago from this place that went out of business down on 4th Street. The guy who owned it always wore these really loud Hawaiian shirts, even in the winter. I always wondered if he was cold. But anyway, no, I haven't really had anything like that with my sleep or feeling super energized. Usually, I'm just tired.
Do you ever hear voices when no one is there?

Well, sometimes... yeah, actually. When the shop is quiet, especially in the late afternoons when the foot traffic dies down, I'll hear this woman muttering my name. It always sounds like it's coming from the polishing room in the back. And it's so strange because that room is right next to the break area where we keep the mini-fridge, and that fridge makes this awful humming noise. I've been meaning to defrost it, but it takes hours and you have to put towels down everywhere. Last time I did it, the water leaked all over the linoleum and warped the edge of it. But anyway, yeah, I hear the voice, and sometimes I'll even smell burning metal, like someone left a torch on, even when I know I shut them all off. It feels so real that I actually have to get up and go check the polishing room to make sure no one is back there.

No, I've never had a seizure. I mean, my hands shake a little bit sometimes if I drink too much coffee, which is the worst when you're trying to set a really small stone. We use these tiny little diamonds called melee, and you have to pick them up with these special tweezers that have a tiny groove in the tip. I actually had to buy a new pair of those tweezers last month because I dropped my old ones on the tile floor at the shop and bent the metal. That tile is so unforgiving. I dropped my favorite mug on it last winter—the one my sister brought back for me from her trip to Sedona. It had these beautiful red rocks painted on it, and it just shattered into a million pieces. I tried to glue it back together with some two-part epoxy we use for pearls, but it just seeps coffee now. It's sitting on my windowsill holding paperclips right now. I really hate throwing things away if I can still find a use for them, you know?
Have you had any recent head injury?

No, no head injuries. I haven't hit my head or anything. I did bump my elbow pretty hard on the edge of the display case last Tuesday, though. The glass on those cases is so thick, you wouldn't think it would hurt that much, but it caught me right on the funny bone. I was actually reaching down to get a piece of lint off the velvet tray—the black velvet shows absolutely everything. We have this little lint roller, but the sticky paper keeps tearing unevenly, so half the time you're just rubbing a piece of cardboard on the jewelry. I told my manager we should just get a new one from the drugstore next door, but he's always trying to save a few cents. He buys our hand soap in these giant gallon jugs that smell like fake green apples, and it dries my skin out so badly. But anyway, no, I haven't bumped my head or had any injuries like that.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you were hearing the woman’s voice even though your mood felt normal—not especially depressed or unusually high?

Yeah, actually, there was a time like that. It was a stretch right before this whole heavy, dark feeling really settled in on me. I was feeling totally normal, you know? I was still running my jewelry making classes in the evenings, and I was even out in my garden every weekend. I grow these incredible heirloom tomatoes—Brandywines and Cherokee Purples. They need so much sun, and you have to stake them really well or the weight of the fruit just snaps the branches right off. I used these old copper pipes I found at a salvage yard to build a trellis for them last year. Copper is so beautiful when it oxidizes and gets that green patina. I actually tried to recreate that patina on a silver pendant once using liver of sulfur, but it smelled like rotten eggs and stunk up the whole shop. But anyway, yeah, for several weeks during that time, my mood was fine, but I kept hearing those noises coming from the polishing room. And I was constantly worrying that customers were standing outside the shop window just watching the business, judging us. It was so distracting when I was trying to teach the classes.
Do you believe that other people are deliberately watching or spying on you?

Well... I know it sounds really odd, but yes. I’ve gotten completely convinced that some of the customers are coming in just to check whether I’ll miss my payments. They just ask way too many questions about the new showroom, you know? My husband keeps saying they’re only being friendly and making conversation, but it feels like they're prying. 

And that new showroom... we just had these custom cherry wood display cases built for it, which cost a fortune. Cherry wood is beautiful, but it is so incredibly temperamental. If you leave a damp cloth on it for even a second, it leaves this terrible white water ring that is nearly impossible to get out. My husband actually set his iced tea down on one of them last week without a coaster, and I had to spend an hour buffing it out with orange oil and a microfiber cloth. I really hate microfiber, honestly. It constantly catches on the rough skin on my hands. When you're working with metal files and polishing compounds all day, your cuticles just get absolutely destroyed. I try to use this heavy-duty shea butter cream at night, but if I put it on during the day, my fingers are way too slippery to grip the jeweler's saw properly. You need a really firm grip when you're piercing sheet metal, otherwise you snap the blades, and those blades are getting so expensive to replace...
Have these problems with hearing the woman’s voice and feeling that customers are watching or prying been going on for at least six months?

Oh, definitely longer than six months. I'd say... well, the voices, those odd smells I catch sometimes, and the worries about the customers watching us... all of that really started around a year and eight months ago. 

I remember because it was right around the time the motor on our main buffing wheel completely burned out. The smell of an electrical motor dying is just awful, it's this sharp, acrid ozone smell that gets right into the back of your throat and just stays there. We had to rush order a new Baldor motor, and the expedited shipping cost almost as much as the unit itself. My husband was furious about the bill, but you really can't compromise on your polishing equipment, you know? If the RPMs aren't exactly right, the jeweler's rouge doesn't cut the metal properly, and you end up with these tiny little drag lines on the silver. I spend hours trying to get a perfect mirror finish on these wide cuff bracelets I make, and any little scratch just ruins the whole piece. I usually have to go back in with a 400-grit sandpaper, then 600, then 800, before I can even think about touching the buffing wheel again. It's so tedious, honestly, and the fine silver dust gets absolutely everywhere. I have this heavy canvas apron that I've worn for maybe fifteen years, and the pockets are practically worn through at the bottom from holding my pliers...
Have you had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Yeah, it's been going on for a while now. Most mornings I wake up with this flat, heavy sadness... it's just like all the color has completely drained out of the house before I even manage to get to the shop. 

Which is hard, because color is everything in my work. I was just sorting through this new parcel of tourmalines I ordered from a dealer I met in Tucson. The Tucson Gem Show is absolutely massive, you know, it basically takes over the entire city every February. We used to go every single year and stay in this little adobe rental near the convention center. The sunsets out there in Arizona are just spectacular, all these burnt oranges and deep purples. But anyway, tourmalines come in literally every shade imaginable. Watermelon tourmaline is usually my favorite—it has this pink center and a green rind, so it literally looks like a tiny slice of watermelon. But it is so incredibly brittle to work with. It has all these natural inclusions, and if you apply even slightly too much pressure with the bezel pusher, the stone just splinters right in the setting. I cracked a gorgeous two-carat piece last month and it just broke my heart. The dealer won't refund you for that, obviously, since it's maker's error. You really have to use a very soft touch and make sure the fine silver is completely annealed before you even try to push it over the stone...
